entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Papirius Crassus was a Roman politician from the Papiria gens (family) in Rome, who played a crucial role in the transformation of the Roman Republic.

Appointed dictator in 340 BC, Crassus' leadership during the Cimber Crisis led to the expulsion of the Cimbrian king and the subsequent Roman victory. He was consul in 336 BC and 330 BC, showcasing his ability to navigate the complexities of Roman politics.

Crassus' legacy extends beyond his military campaigns; he also played a significant role in the development of Roman law and governance. His policies and actions influenced the Roman Republic's trajectory, ultimately contributing to its transformation into the Roman Empire.

Crassus' influence can still be seen in the modern-day concept of 'crassness,' which refers to excessive ambition and ruthlessness in politics. His name has become synonymous with these traits, serving as a cautionary tale for politicians and leaders throughout history.
